title: Last minute advice for YC applicants: six tips from Garry Tan
summary: Garry Tan's 2014 advice to YC applicants covers who should apply, how to pick a problem, team composition, writing clearly, getting feedback and not waiting for permission. The core lessons apply to any early startup: solve a real problem or do it right, pair a builder with a hustler, and write in plain English.

principles.text: Pick a hair-on-fire problem nobody has solved, or solve an existing problem so much better that it is done right.
principles.quote: They either solve a hair on fire problem that has never been solved before OR they solve a problem that has other solutions, but they do it so much better that they are "done right."

principles.text: Technology has no value on its own. It only matters when it solves people's problems.
principles.quote: Great hackers get caught up in technology, but technology doesn't create value in and of itself. Technology is only useful for solving people's problems.

principles.text: If you are new, explain what you are. If you are not new, explain how you are different.
principles.quote: If you're new, focus on explaining what you are. If you're not new, focus on explaining how you're different. If you're neither of these types, you're doing it wrong.

principles.text: A strong founding team needs both a builder and a hustler. Builders alone can't reach users and hustlers alone can't make product.
principles.quote: I've seen teams of hustlers fail because they can't create any product on their own. I've seen teams of pure builders (amazing designer / engineers) that fail because they can't put the product in the hands of users.

principles.text: Unclear writing signals unclear thinking. Write everything down, then edit mercilessly in plain English, not corporate speak.
principles.quote: If a founder can't express their ideas clearly to others, then the simplest and likeliest explanation is actually that the idea is not particularly clear to them either.

principles.text: Don't wait for permission. Keep building the startup whether or not an accelerator accepts you.
principles.quote: You've got to keep working on the startup no matter what. Realize that you don't need anyone to give you a permission slip to create your own startup.
